applicationInfo.name: Threat Model Export
applicationInfo.description: Advisory, read-only serverless pipeline that detects exposed/compromised AWS access keys from AWS Health, Security Hub (GuardDuty), and Trusted Advisor, then invokes AWS DevOps Agent (via an HMAC-signed Agent Space webhook) to investigate 90 days of CloudTrail activity and produce human-run containment recommendations. It sends heads-up notifications (SNS email, optional Slack/Teams). It never mutates customer resources.

mitigations.content: HMAC-SHA256 request signing on the webhook with a strong secret; enforce timestamp/nonce freshness to prevent replay
Scope EventBridge to reserved AWS sources and validate/normalize event fields before use
Validate and sanitize the agent's Markdown report against the output contract; encode output before rendering
Comprehensive audit logging: CloudTrail, Step Functions history, structured Lambda logs with failure context
Minimize and protect PII in notifications and logs; encrypt SNS; restrict subscribers and log access
Store secrets in Secrets Manager with a customer-managed KMS CMK; scope GetSecretValue and kms:Decrypt to specific ARNs
Reserved concurrency + SQS DLQ with redrive; alarm on DLQ depth and throttles
Graceful failure handling with SNS fallback plus bounded retry/backoff and delivery-failure alarms
Accept unavoidable Resource:* on Organizations/Account read APIs; compensate with read-only role, monitoring, and anomaly alarms
Advisory-only design: no auto-mutation; human-in-the-loop performs all containment
Protect IaC/code/KMS policy with least-privilege deploy roles, review, and change monitoring; avoid CLI secret exposure

businessContext.description: Advisory, read-only serverless pipeline that detects exposed/compromised AWS access keys from AWS Health, Security Hub (GuardDuty), and Trusted Advisor, then invokes AWS DevOps Agent (via an HMAC-signed Agent Space webhook) to investigate 90 days of CloudTrail activity and produce human-run containment recommendations. It sends heads-up notifications (SNS email, optional Slack/Teams). It never mutates customer resources.

components.name: EventBridge Detection Rules
components.description: Three rules matching aws.health (AWS_RISK_CREDENTIALS_EXPOSED), aws.securityhub (AwsIamAccessKey ACTIVE/NEW findings), and aws.trustedadvisor (Exposed Access Keys) on the default event bus; targets the EventRouter Lambda.

components.name: EventRouter Lambda
components.description: Python 3.12/ARM64. Parses the source event into a normalized incident, enriches with read-only account context (Organizations + Account alternate contacts), and starts the Step Functions execution. Read-only w.r.t. customer resources.

components.name: Investigation State Machine
components.description: Two-state workflow: InvokeAgent (Callback Lambda) then HeadsUpNotify (Notifier Lambda).

components.name: Callback Lambda
components.description: Invokes the AWS DevOps Agent Space webhook over HMAC-signed HTTPS to start an investigation, passing the incident and callback task token. Also parses the agent's Markdown report on callback. HTTPS-only enforced.

components.name: Notifier Lambda
components.description: Publishes heads-up and findings notifications to SNS (email) and optional Slack/Teams incoming webhooks (HTTPS-only). Falls back to SNS if chat delivery fails.

components.name: AWS DevOps Agent Space
components.description: Managed agent that receives the HMAC-signed webhook, runs the access-key-compromise investigation skill (read-only CloudTrail/IAM/resource describe), and surfaces findings + human-run recommendations in its operator app.

components.name: SNS Alerts Topic
components.description: Email-subscribed topic used as the reliable notification fallback. Encrypted with the aws/sns managed key.

components.name: KMS CMK
components.description: Customer-managed key with rotation enabled; encrypts the two Secrets Manager secrets and the SQS DLQ. Key policy grants secretsmanager/sqs/lambda service principals Decrypt+GenerateDataKey.

components.name: Slack/Teams Webhooks
components.description: Optional external chat sinks reached over HTTPS using bearer-style webhook URLs held in Secrets Manager.

components.name: Security Responder (operator)
components.description: Human engineer who reviews findings in the DevOps Agent operator app and manually runs containment steps. All mutation is human-performed, outside this system.

connections.description: EventBridge invokes EventRouter Lambda on a matching detection event (async, AWS-internal).
EventRouter calls states:StartExecution with the normalized incident.
EventRouter reads read-only account context via Organizations DescribeAccount/ListTagsForResource and Account GetAlternateContact.
State machine invokes Callback Lambda (InvokeAgent state).
State machine invokes Notifier Lambda (HeadsUpNotify state).
Callback reads the HMAC secret from Secrets Manager (GetSecretValue).
Callback POSTs the HMAC-signed incident to the DevOps Agent Space webhook (external HTTPS egress).
Notifier reads Slack/Teams webhook URLs from Secrets Manager (GetSecretValue).
Notifier publishes to the SNS Alerts topic (sns:Publish).
Notifier POSTs the heads-up message to optional Slack/Teams webhooks (external HTTPS egress).
SNS delivers the email notification to the subscribed security responder.
Responder reviews findings/recommendations in the DevOps Agent operator app and manually runs containment.
Failed async invocations of the Lambdas are routed to the SQS DLQ.
KMS CMK encrypts/decrypts the Channels secret.
KMS CMK encrypts the SQS DLQ messages.

dataStores.name: WebhookSecret (Secrets Manager)
dataStores.description: HMAC signing secret for the DevOps Agent webhook. CMK-encrypted. NoEcho parameter at deploy time.

dataStores.name: Channels Secret (Secrets Manager)
dataStores.description: JSON of Slack/Teams webhook URLs (bearer-style secrets). CMK-encrypted.

dataStores.name: Dead Letter Queue (SQS)
dataStores.description: Captures failed async Lambda invocations for 14 days for manual redrive. CMK-encrypted. Holds incident payloads (access key IDs, account context).

dataStores.name: CloudWatch Logs
dataStores.description: Structured logs from the three Lambdas. May contain incident fields (access key IDs, account IDs); code truncates payloads and avoids logging full webhook URLs.

trustZones.name: AWS Event Sources
trustZones.description: AWS Health, Security Hub/GuardDuty, and Trusted Advisor emitting onto the default EventBridge bus. AWS-managed but the event payload content is attacker-influenceable (e.g., exposure location, principal fields).

trustZones.name: Pipeline Account (deployed stack)
trustZones.description: The customer AWS account boundary containing the SAM stack: EventBridge rules, the three Lambdas, Step Functions, SNS, KMS CMK, Secrets Manager secrets, and the SQS DLQ.

trustZones.name: AWS DevOps Agent Space
trustZones.description: Managed AWS DevOps Agent service that receives the webhook and runs the read-only investigation skill.

trustZones.name: External Chat Providers
trustZones.description: Slack and Microsoft Teams - third-party SaaS reached over the public internet via incoming webhook URLs.

trustZones.name: Human Responder
trustZones.description: The security engineer who reviews findings and manually performs any containment. Outside the automated system.

crossingPoints.description: Detection events cross from AWS event sources into the pipeline account via EventBridge rule matching then async Lambda invoke.
Callback Lambda egresses from the pipeline account to the DevOps Agent Space webhook over HMAC-signed HTTPS.
Notifier Lambda egresses from the pipeline account to external Slack/Teams over the public internet using bearer-style webhook URLs.
Pipeline notifies the human responder (SNS email) and the responder reviews findings in the DevOps Agent operator app.

assets.name: Compromise incident payload
assets.description: Normalized incident: exposed access key ID, principal, account ID, detection source, timestamp, and enriched account context.

assets.name: Account alternate contacts (PII)
assets.description: Operations/Security/Billing contact names, emails, phone numbers plus account name/email/tags, resolved read-only for notification routing.

assets.name: Webhook HMAC secret
assets.description: Signing secret proving the webhook POST originates from this pipeline.

assets.name: Chat webhook URLs
assets.description: Slack/Teams incoming webhook URLs, bearer-style secrets embedded in the URL path.

assets.name: Investigation report
assets.description: Agent's Markdown report: CloudTrail activity, affected resources, severity, and human-run containment recommendations.

flows.description: Detection event carrying the (attacker-influenceable) incident fields enters the pipeline via EventBridge.
EventRouter reads account PII via Organizations/Account APIs and folds it into the incident carried into Step Functions.
Callback reads the HMAC secret from Secrets Manager (CMK-decrypted) to sign the webhook.
Callback POSTs the HMAC-signed incident to the external DevOps Agent Space webhook.
Notifier reads Slack/Teams webhook URLs from Secrets Manager (CMK-decrypted).
Notifier posts the report/heads-up (containing incident + report content) to external Slack/Teams over the public internet.
Notifier publishes the notification to the SNS topic for email delivery.
SNS delivers the email (containing account PII + incident summary) to the subscribed responder.
On failure the incident payload is routed to the CMK-encrypted SQS DLQ.

softwareProfile.description: AWS SAM stack: 3 EventBridge rules -> EventRouter Lambda -> Step Functions -> Callback Lambda (HMAC-signed HTTPS webhook to AWS DevOps Agent Space) -> Notifier Lambda (SNS + optional Slack/Teams). CMK-encrypted Secrets Manager secrets and SQS DLQ. Python 3.12 on ARM64. Read-only IAM only.

userPersonas.description: AWS Health, Security Hub (GuardDuty), and Trusted Advisor emit events onto the default event bus that match the 3 EventBridge rules and trigger the EventRouter Lambda.

nonFunctionalRequirements.rationale: Detection-to-investigation trigger completes in seconds; investigation itself runs asynchronously in the managed agent.
Serverless (Lambda, Step Functions, EventBridge) with an SQS DLQ capturing failed invocations for redrive.
Failed events land in a 14-day-retention SQS DLQ for manual redrive; stack is redeployable via SAM.
Advisory-only by design: on any failure or ambiguity the pipeline notifies humans and takes no mutating action.
Feeds incident-response decisions for compromised credentials; incorrect or missing findings could delay containment.
Regex/Markdown parsing of the agent output contract and event parsing must degrade gracefully rather than crash the pipeline.
